content_units: Best First Watch for Your Tastes

You’ll likely enjoy the titles that combine   clear character growth  ,   strong emotional payoff  ,   low fan service  , and a   finished, manageable run  . For a busy adult with about   5 hours per week  , the best first pick is   Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood   because it delivers the most complete balance of payoff, pacing, and closure.
Ranked Watch Order
Option 1:   Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood     Best overall match: finished, emotionally rewarding, consistently strong character arcs     Top pick

-   Why watch first:   It hits your priorities almost perfectly: major character growth, powerful emotional turns, very little distracting fan service, and a fully completed story with a satisfying ending.
-   Pros:   Excellent ensemble cast; emotional stakes build steadily; tight payoff; action and drama stay balanced.
-   Possible downsides:   It is longer than some others here, so it’s a medium commitment even though it’s finished.
Watch first
Option 2:   Mob Psycho 100     Outstanding character growth with heart, humor, and a complete story     Best shorter modern pick
-   Why it ranks high:   Few anime handle personal growth better. The emotional core is sincere, the fan service is basically negligible, and the story is complete.
-   Pros:   One of the best growth arcs in anime; surprisingly moving; visually inventive; easy to watch in chunks.
-   Possible downsides:   The exaggerated art style can take a few episodes to click if you prefer more polished realism.
Option 3:   Steins;Gate     Slow-burn setup that pays off with some of the strongest emotional and character payoff in anime     Best if you want intensity
-   Why it fits:   The second half delivers huge emotional payoff and strong development, especially if you enjoy tension, consequence, and character-driven sci-fi.
-   Pros:   Excellent payoff; memorable cast dynamics; finished main story; emotionally gripping once it gets going.
-   Possible downsides:   The early episodes are notably slow, and there is a bit more awkward anime humor than in your top-fit titles.
Option 4:   Haikyuu!!     Extremely likable cast and uplifting growth across a long but rewarding sports journey     Best comfort watch
-   Why it works:   Character growth is one of its biggest strengths, and the emotional highs are very real without relying on fan service.
-   Pros:   Easy to keep watching; deeply lovable cast; energizing and positive; low fan service.
-   Possible downsides:   It’s a bigger time investment, and depending on how strictly you define “finished,” it may feel less tidy as a first choice than the fully self-contained picks above.
Option 5:   Violet Evergarden     Beautiful, emotional, and mature with excellent personal healing themes     Best if you want something reflective
-   Why it fits:   Very strong emotional payoff and character growth, with a polished, adult-friendly tone and little to no fan service.
-   Pros:   Gorgeous production; emotionally rich; easy to watch in weekly doses; strong central arc.
-   Possible downsides:   More introspective and episodic in feel, so it may not hook you as strongly if you want momentum and plot drive first.
Option 6:   Cowboy Bebop     Stylish classic with mature tone and excellent atmosphere     Best for mood over growth
-   Why it’s lower for your tastes:   It’s great, but compared with the others, it is less centered on continuous visible character growth and more about mood, themes, and episodic storytelling.
-   Pros:   Mature, cool, iconic, finished, low fan service; very easy to sample.
-   Possible downsides:   The emotional payoff is more subtle and detached than the stronger growth-focused picks above.
Best Starting Pick for 5 Hours per Week
Start with: Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood
- At 5 hours per week, you can comfortably watch around   6–7 episodes weekly  .
- That makes it a very manageable completed series with steady momentum and frequent payoff.
- It is the safest recommendation if you want   one show that strongly satisfies all your stated preferences  .
If you want the strongest alternatives by mood:
-   Most character growth:   Mob Psycho 100
-   Most emotional sci-fi payoff:   Steins;Gate
-   Most soothing emotional watch:   Violet Evergarden
Quick Watch Strategy
-   Watch first:   Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood
-   Watch next:   Mob Psycho 100 if you want another completed, growth-heavy series right after
-   Save for later:   Haikyuu!! when you’re ready for a longer uplifting commitment
